newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU women having more babies again.
newsitem.headline: EU women having more babies again.

text.p: Women in the European Union are having more babies again, for the first time since 1990.

Women in the 15-country bloc now have an average 1.44 children in their lifetime, but this is still only fractionally up from a post-war record low of 1.43 in 1995, the EU's statistical office said on Friday.
The number of children born also rose to just over 4 million babies last year from just under 4 million in 1995, the lowest figure since 1945.
Births have been declining since the 1960s as a result of the sexual revolution and an increase in women postponing motherhood or having no children.
The EU's fertility rate is similar to Japan's and that of most other developed countries, but far below the United States average of 2.06 babies for each woman.
Inside the EU, Ireland posted the highest fertility rate at 1.91, with Spain the lowest at 1.15.
